channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Iran Arrests Japan Public Broadcaster's Bureau Chief In Tehran
item.description: Iran has arrested the bureau chief of Japan's public broadcaster, NHK World, and transferred him to Tehran’s notorious Evin Prison, two sources told RFE/RL's Radio Farda.

item.title: Student Protests Continue To Spread Across Tehran
item.description: University students across the Iranian capital turned out for a fourth day of renewed anti-government protests on February 24, following a brutal state crackdown in January. Thousands of people were killed last month in protests sparked by economic collapse and oppression in Iran.

item.title: Trump Vows In Address To 'Never Allow' Iran To Have Nuclear Weapons.
item.description: US President Donald Trump used the longest State of the Union address in US history to repeat the threat of military action against Iran if diplomacy fails -- and pledged to keep negotiating to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Popular Iranian Actor Flees Homeland After Deadly Crackdown On Protests
item.description: Iranian actor Amirali Danaei has left Iran, denouncing the Islamic republic as a dictatorship after a deadly crackdown on protests. Once a state-TV star, he now vows never to work under the clerical system again, calling the crisis a human tragedy where “human lives are not up for negotiation.”

item.title: In State Of The Union Address, Trump Vows To Block Iran's Nuclear Ambitions
item.description: US President Donald Trump delivered his State of the Union address before a joint session of Congress on February 24. As a US military buildup continues in the Middle East, raising fears of a conflict with Iran, Trump said that he will "never allow" Iran to acquire a nuclear weapon.

item.title: Filmmaker Ilanlou Says Iran Is 'A Patient In The Throes of Death'
item.description: Documentary filmmaker and activist Mojgan Ilanlou says Iran is like “a patient in the throes of death,” warning that the country’s social and economic crises have spread beyond traditional fault lines.

item.title: Iranian Students Reject Virtual Classrooms As Protests Spread
item.description: As university students in Iran continued their fifth day of protests in the wake of January's brutal crackdown, demonstrators insisted they will keep showing up in person on campus despite an effort to promote virtual classrooms.

item.title: Son Of UK Motorcyclist Held In Iran Urges 'Compassion' During Ramadan
item.description: Lindsay and Craig Foreman were arrested while traveling through Iran on a motorcycle trip in 2025. This February, they were sentenced to 10 years in prison on espionage charges. Lindsay''s son, Joe Bennett, has called on the Iranian government to use the month of Ramadan to exercise mercy.

item.title: US, Iran To Meet For Nuclear Talks Amid Fears Of Military Conflict
item.description: US and Iranian officials are set to hold a fresh round of nuclear talks in Geneva on February 26 for what is seen as a last-ditch attempt to avoid a major military conflict between the foes.

item.title: Trump, Zelenskyy Speak By Phone Ahead Of Geneva Talks As Pressure Mounts For Tougher Line On Russia
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke by phone on February 25, a high-stakes conversation confirmed by both the White House and Kyiv as diplomatic efforts intensify ahead of renewed negotiations in Geneva.
